Safeguards and intended use

John Hazelton · Independent recruiting operations portfolio · Updated 5 November 2026

What this tool does

Fixed rules identify missing fields, inconsistent records and delayed operational steps. Priority labels concern data repairs, never candidate quality. Findings and root-cause hypotheses require human verification in the source ATS. Nothing updates the ATS automatically.

Candidate IDs, not candidate profiles

Prepare a CSV containing only necessary operational fields and opaque application and candidate IDs. Names, emails, phone numbers, CVs, notes and unrecognised columns are discarded before retained audit state is created. The original selected file is necessarily read temporarily by the browser; prepare a minimised export first and do not include sensitive data.

Imports retain IDs, recognised statuses, timestamps and presence indicators for source and rejection reason. Role titles and stage names become local references. Duplicate flags use candidate ID plus role, and require manual review. IDs and operational histories remain personal data if linkable to a person: this is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation. ID syntax checks cannot prove that an ID contains no personal information.

Local processing and exports

Uploaded file contents are processed in browser memory and are not sent to Supabase, analytics or an AI model. Reload or Clear data removes the app’s working references; this does not guarantee forensic memory erasure. Downloaded repair queues contain pseudonymous personal data. Keep them in authorised systems, share with appropriate staff and apply your organisation’s retention policy. The original file and downloads are not deleted by Clear data.

AI and employment decisions

No model runs inside this app. The optional external review brief uses fixed aggregate categories, suppresses counts below five and buckets other totals. It excludes candidate IDs, record details and raw text. Aggregation does not guarantee anonymity; review the remaining context and use an approved provider before sharing.

Do not use this demonstration to score suitability, shortlist, reject, profile candidates, infer protected traits or make employment decisions. Adding or using AI for those purposes requires a fresh assessment under the EU AI Act and applicable US federal, state and local employment rules. Human approval alone does not remove legal obligations.

Before using real operational data

  • Document the purpose, lawful basis, authorised staff and minimum export fields.
  • Provide appropriate privacy information and a route for people to exercise their rights.
  • Review hosting and processor terms, international transfers, security and retention. Decide whether a DPIA is required.
  • Validate rule accuracy and coverage using a representative pseudonymised export. Review false positives and source records before acting.
  • Assess the intended deployment and jurisdiction with qualified counsel before production employment use.

Visitor analytics

Optional usage analytics begins only after consent. It stores allowlisted section and action names, estimated active time and random visit identifiers for 30 days. The application stores no IP address or IP network in analytics. Hosting and Supabase infrastructure still receive connection metadata and may retain operational logs. Rejecting analytics has no effect on diagnostics. See analytics privacy details.

Limits and contact

These are implemented engineering safeguards, not a GDPR, EU AI Act or US legal compliance certification. A fictional demonstration is not an approval for production hiring use. Contact John Hazelton privately about privacy requests; do not send candidate records.

Official references: GDPR, EU AI Act, NYC automated employment decision tools, Illinois Public Act 103-0804, CNIL audience measurement guidance.
